name: @withicons/mcp

tools.name: search_icons
tools.description: Find icons by meaning. Understands plain English, synonyms, plurals, phrases and typos ("trash can", "throw away", "settigns", "money"). Returns ranked exact matches (icon name, title, category, confidence, why it matched, page url and a ready-to-paste snippet); didYouMean when the query was spell-corrected. When no icon carries the words it says noExactMatch and lists a few similar icons under additional (loosely related, never with a snippet): use one only if it fits, otherwise try a simpler word or browse a category. A hint says where to browse when nothing is close; suggestions (names a typo away) appear only when a name really is close. Snippets: every exact match carries one in structuredContent (in the format you ask for, default react) and the text shows the first one only; format "none" returns names only, with no snippet in either, so pick a name here and call get_icon for the code (use it for lists, comparisons and long queries; svg snippets are large).

query.description: What the icon should show, in plain words

format.description: Snippet format (default react), or "none" for names only: no snippet in the result or the text

tools.name: get_icon
tools.description: Get one icon as paste-ready code or SVG. name takes a canonical name or an alias ("delete" -> trash). format: svg, react, vue, svelte, angular, solid, html-class, web-component, data-uri (default svg). Colours: palette (an id from list_palettes) and/or colors (roles ink, c1-c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge -> hex; merged over the palette); theme puts brand colours on this icon's own parts; color replaces currentColor in svg / data-uri; flat bakes the CSS variables into the svg (for , Figma, slides). The result has colors.mainRole (the colour role that paints the largest part, measured on the render) and colors.roleAreas (each role's share), warnings (colours that change nothing in this style), notes (e.g. a colour this style paints only as a see-through tone), appliedTheme (where each theme colour went; exact: primary shows unmixed), motion (whether animate_icon has a tuned animation) and, with include_palettes (default: a palette style with no format), the icon palette ids. list_styles says which roles each style paints.

flat.description: svg only: bake CSS-variable colours into the file (for , Figma, slides, rasterizers)

palette.description: Apply one of the icon colour palettes by id (see colors.suggestions in the result, or list_palettes), e.g. "classic-red"

colors.description: Change any colour: roles ink (outline), c1 (main), c2, c3, c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge -> "#hex" or a CSS colour name; also accepts --with-* variable names. Merged over palette (or theme). Which roles a style paints: list_styles colours.

theme.description: Brand colours (hex): "#0ea5e9" or { primary, secondary?, tertiary?, ink? }, put on each icon's own parts by size (primary on the largest part, secondary the next, tertiary the third; further parts, tint and shadow take primary's hue) in any style, so one theme fits a mixed set. Exact hex (flat): line, solid, duo, gloss, engrave, blueprint, sketch, sticker, retro, bauhaus, anime, pastel, brutal; shaded (gradients, see-through tones or shading, so the hex is one tone of several): glass, kawaii, pixel, luxe, skeuo, gothic, coquette, plush, clay, bento, suite, dock, liquid, chrome, soft3d, utsav, rangoli, halloween, christmas, lunar, valentine. Not with palette.

include_palettes.description: List the icon's palette ids (colors.suggestions). Default: only for a palette style when no format is given

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description: The 34 visual styles every icon is drawn in (line, solid, duo, gloss, engrave, blueprint, sketch, glass, kawaii, sticker, pixel, retro, luxe, bauhaus, skeuo, anime, gothic, pastel, coquette, plush, clay, bento, suite, dock, liquid, chrome, soft3d, brutal, utsav, rangoli, halloween, christmas, lunar, valentine), with their group (Essentials, Product & brand, 3D & glass, Playful, Artistic, Holidays), goodFor, what each looks like, minSize (the smallest px it reads well at: 16 for UI styles, 32 creative and palette, 48 studio and storybook) and onDark (how to use it on dark backgrounds); palette styles list their colour variables. Every style has colours: the roles its icons really paint, read from the rendered icons (each role's variables, whether it is a solid, see-through tone or gradient fill / stroke, on how many icons; empty for one-colour styles), and exact (whether a brand hex shows unmixed, see theme on get_icon / export_icon).

tools.name: recommend_styles
tools.description: Which style(s) to use for a job. for: plain words about what you are making ("Diwali sale banner", "avatar picker for a kids app", "animated 3D icons for an AI landing page", "admin dashboard", "Christmas email"); or use: one of the "What are you making?" ids from withicons.com. Ranks by your own words: a festival named in for wins ("Halloween party app" -> halloween, "Christmas email" -> christmas, "Diwali sale" -> rangoli, utsav), then the job (AI, SaaS, kids, print ...) and look words (isometric, claymorphism, neo-brutalism); use: "festive" lists every festival with its style. Returns ranked styles, each with its group, what it is good for, the React import, <with-icon> and class snippets, the npm packages holding its raw files, its download-all zip, 3D motion support, holiday palettes and Duo presets; plus festival icon categories, avatar advice (inclusive skin-tone palettes) and notes. Several festivals named ("Diwali, Eid, Holi and Christmas"): styles rank by how many of them each covers, and a note says which style covers which festival (and that Eid has none): use a festival style per festival, or one neutral style across them. "Exact brand colours", a brand palette or a hex in for: flat styles (solid, line, duo ...) rank first, each entry says exactColours true or false, and a note says gradient and shadow styles cannot match a hex exactly. compact: true returns per style only the name, group, what it suits and the React and <with-icon> snippets (no palettes, packages, presets or downloads; about a third of the size). Then search_icons / get_icon(name, style) for the icons themselves.

for.description: What you are making, in plain words

use.description: A job id: app (An app or website), slides (Slides and documents), saas (A SaaS landing page), ai (An AI product), brand (Something premium), kids (Something playful), print (Print or editorial), festive (A festival or seasonal campaign)

icon.description: Icon the snippets show (default home), e.g. "diya" or "avatar-woman"

compact.description: Short answer: per style only name, group, what it suits and the React and <with-icon> snippets, with no palette lists, packages, presets or downloads (default false)

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: All icon categories with counts, or (with category) every icon in that category. Festival icons: indian-festivals (Diwali, Holi, Durga Puja), christmas, lunar-new-year, valentines, halloween; avatars: people (true-to-life skin-tone and hair palettes via list_palettes), animals and friendly monsters; ai: AI and assistant icons.

category.description: List the icons in this category

tools.name: resolve_icon
tools.description: Check whether a name or alias maps to exactly one icon. Returns the canonical name (status resolved), the ambiguous candidates, a match by meaning (status synonym: a word that is not a name or alias but means an icon, e.g. "favourites" -> star / heart, "orders" -> receipt; with candidates and a note; use the canonical name), or for unknown words the nearest names, didYouMean (a spelling correction) and a hint.

tools.name: list_palettes
tools.description: The 20-30 colour palettes picked for one icon (true-to-life first, then moods: pastel, neon, retro, earthy, luxe, ...), each with its ten role colours (ink, c1-c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge). With a style, every palette also lists the exact CSS variables it sets on that icon in that style, the icon variables with their roles and defaults, mainRole (the colour role that paints the largest part of the icon, measured on the render, e.g. c2) and roleAreas (each role's share of the drawn icon). Multi-colour styles: glass, kawaii, sticker, pixel, retro, luxe, bauhaus, skeuo, anime, gothic, pastel, coquette, plush, clay, bento, suite, dock, liquid, chrome, soft3d, brutal, utsav, rangoli, halloween, christmas, lunar, valentine, plus duo and blueprint (their roles: list_styles); one-colour styles only take the ink. Apply one with get_icon(name, style, format, palette: "<id>"); for brand colours across a set use theme (get_icon / export_icon).

style.description: Style to map the palettes onto (e.g. kawaii, sticker, retro)

tag.description: Only palettes with this tag (true-to-life, pastel, vivid, neon, earthy, retro, vintage, mono, grayscale, dark, on-dark, luxe, seasonal, nature, ocean, sunset, candy, accessible, corporate, y2k)

tools.name: animate_icon
tools.description: Paste-ready animation code for an icon, using the optional @withicons/motion package (CSS, works with every style and package). trigger: loop = continuous (spinner, ringing bell), hover = one-shot on hover/focus (or of a .wm-trigger button), once = plays on load, inview = plays when scrolled into view, swap = the icon turns into another one (play -> pause, menu -> close, heart -> heart@solid). Icons with a tuned motion use it by default; preset overrides it. The result has intent (what the motion shows), alternates (other tuned presets of this icon, e.g. a livelier one for a title slide) and lively (the most energetic presets); pass one as preset. 750 icons have tuned motion. Pass the style the page uses: 3D styles (clay, glass, liquid, chrome, soft3d, luxe, skeuo, dock, plush) play the motion in 3D (the code adds wm-3d, motion3d: true) and the result lists moves: the moves the icon offers in that style (soft3d: 3-5, e.g. pop-up, press, hop, turn, gleam); pass one as preset. For a moving icon as a FILE (slides, docs, email, social) use export_icon with format gif, apng, animated-svg, pptx-animated or lottie and the same motion (motion: "loop", "hover", "swap" or a preset).

trigger.description: loop (default), hover, once, inview or swap

preset.description: Override the motion (e.g. spin, ring, beat, float, bounce, pop)

to.description: swap only: target icon, "name" or "name@style" (default: the icon's suggested swap)

effect.description: swap only: transition (default from the spec, else fade)

tools.name: export_icon
tools.description: Make icon FILES (not code) for slides, documents, design tools, apps and social posts. Animated: gif (plays everywhere; set background to the slide colour), apng, animated-svg, pptx-animated (a ready 16:9 slide), lottie / dotlottie; motion picks the movement. Still: svg, svg-flat (colours baked in), pdf, eps, png, png-set, ico, favicon-pack, android, ios, pptx, pptx-sheet (every style), docx, and code (jsx, tsx, vue, svelte, html, css, data-uri ...). Files are saved to out_dir when given and returned inline when small. Colours are baked in: set palette / colors / color, or theme (brand colours put on each icon's own parts, in any style) and per_icon (different colours for some icons) here. Several icons: names: ["home", "settings"], or a map { "receipt": "orders" } to name each file; icons without the palette borrow it from the first that has it, matched by part size (strict_palette: true fails instead). colorReport says per icon and style which colours changed nothing there (ignored), where the theme colours went (and whether primary shows exactly) and what a borrowed palette put on which part; warnings come first. File names default to <name>-<style>[-<variant>].<ext>; filename takes a template ({name} {style} {format} {variant} {default}) or an exact name.

names.description: List, or map icon -> file base name

format.description: One format or a comma list (see the tool description). Slides and docs: png at size 512, transparent, embedded as a picture (PNG, not SVG)

filename.description: Template or exact name; extension added

matte.description: gif: edge colour to blend with, kept transparent

strict_palette.description: Fail when an icon lacks the palette

colors.description: Role -> colour (ink, c1-c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge); wins over theme

theme.description: Brand colours (hex): "#0ea5e9" or { primary, secondary?, tertiary?, ink? }, put on each icon's own parts by size (primary on the largest part, secondary the next, tertiary the third; further parts, tint and shadow take primary's hue) in any style, so one theme fits a mixed set. Exact hex (flat): line, solid, duo, gloss, engrave, blueprint, sketch, sticker, retro, bauhaus, anime, pastel, brutal; shaded (gradients, see-through tones or shading, so the hex is one tone of several): glass, kawaii, pixel, luxe, skeuo, gothic, coquette, plush, clay, bento, suite, dock, liquid, chrome, soft3d, utsav, rangoli, halloween, christmas, lunar, valentine. Not with palette.

per_icon.description: Colours for single icons, over theme: { "heart": "#e11d48", "star": { "primary": "#f59e0b", "secondary": "#fde68a" } } (a string is the primary); role keys (c1 ...) set that role on that icon only, e.g. keep a people avatar's skin (c1; hair c2, clothes c4): { "avatar-woman": { "c1": "#f6d2b6" } }. Names among the exported icons.

motion.description: loop (default), hover, once, swap, none or a preset

hold.description: swap: seconds to rest on each icon

seconds.description: gif / apng loop length in seconds

padding.description: Space around the icon, share of its size

out_dir.description: Folder to save the files in

tools.name: preview_icons
tools.description: Look before you choose: one labelled picture of several icons in several styles. Rows are icons (names or aliases, 1-24), columns are styles (1-6, default line); with one style it is a gallery (columns = icons per row). Palette styles show their default colours; palette (an id from list_palettes) or colors { c1, ink, ... } previews a brand colour. size: icon size in px (12-256, default 64; use 16-24 to see how it reads in a UI). background: light (default), dark (outlines turn light) or a hex colour. labels: false for the bare grid. A style below its minSize (list_styles) still renders, with a note. Returns a PNG as image content (format: "svg" for the vector sheet); out_dir also saves it. Then get_icon(name, style, format) for the code of the icon you pick. Styles: line, solid, duo, gloss, engrave, blueprint, sketch, glass, kawaii, sticker, pixel, retro, luxe, bauhaus, skeuo, anime, gothic, pastel, coquette, plush, clay, bento, suite, dock, liquid, chrome, soft3d, brutal, utsav, rangoli, halloween, christmas, lunar, valentine.

names.description: Icons to show, one row each (name or alias, 1-24), e.g. ["cake", "cookie", "donut"]

styles.description: Styles to compare, one column each (1-6; default ["line"]), e.g. ["line", "duo", "clay", "kawaii"]

style.description: Shortcut for one style (as in get_icon); styles is the list

background.description: "light" (default), "dark" (light outlines) or a hex colour such as "#fde68a"

labels.description: Write the icon names and style names on the sheet (default true)

columns.description: One style only: icons per row (default: balanced, at most 6)

palette.description: Palette id (list_palettes): shown on the icons that have it

colors.description: Role -> colour (ink, c1-c4, tint, accent, shadow, shine, edge) for a brand preview

format.description: png (default: an image you can see) or svg

out_dir.description: Folder to save the sheet in

instructions:
with icons (withicons.com): 750 open-source (MIT) icons, each drawn in 34 styles, in 6 groups: Essentials (line, solid, duo, suite); Product & brand (bento, dock, brutal, bauhaus); 3D & glass (clay, glass, liquid, chrome, soft3d, luxe, skeuo); Playful (kawaii, plush, sticker, gloss, pastel, pixel, retro); Artistic (sketch, engrave, blueprint, anime, gothic, coquette); Holidays (utsav, rangoli, halloween, christmas, lunar, valentine).
Workflow: search_icons with what the icon should show ("delete", "throw away", "user settings") -> pick a name -> get_icon(name, style, format) for paste-ready code.
Look before you choose: preview_icons(names, styles) returns ONE labelled picture (a PNG) of several icons in several styles, rows = icons, columns = styles, optionally on a dark or brand-colour background; use it to compare styles and pick between candidates instead of guessing.
Choosing a style: recommend_styles(for: "what you are making", e.g. "Diwali sale banner", "avatar picker for a kids app", "AI landing page") returns the best styles with packages, snippets, presets and palettes. Best per job: an app or website: line, duo, solid, suite; slides and documents: solid, duo, suite, clay; a saas landing page: bento, soft3d, duo, dock; an ai product: clay, liquid, chrome, glass; something premium: glass, luxe, chrome, dock; something playful: kawaii, plush, sticker, gloss; print or editorial: engrave, sketch, blueprint, bauhaus; a festival or seasonal campaign: rangoli, christmas, halloween, lunar. One style per page or UI region; only line, solid and duo go in 16-24px controls, the others at 32px+.
Festivals: icon categories indian-festivals, christmas, lunar-new-year, valentines, halloween plus holiday styles with festival palettes. Avatars: category avatars (people with true-to-life skin-tone and hair palettes: offer several; animals; friendly monsters). Style words in a query pick the style ("cute heart" -> kawaii, "8-bit star" -> pixel, "isometric server" -> soft3d, "claymorphism" -> clay, "manga" -> anime, "toy" or "kids" -> plush).
Colours: line, solid, gloss, engrave, sketch draw in one colour (currentColor: set color); the others paint colour roles as CSS variables with defaults (the ink follows currentColor). list_styles gives each style's roles as its icons paint them (duo: c1 = a 20% tone fill (648 of 750 icons), accent = a solid stroke (521 of 750 icons); blueprint: c1 = a solid stroke). Each icon has 20-30 colour palettes picked for it: list_palettes(name, style) shows them; get_icon / export_icon take palette: "<id>" or colors: { c1, c2, ink, ... }. Brand colours: theme: { primary, secondary?, tertiary?, ink? } (hex) puts them on each icon's own parts, largest first, in any style (per_icon on export_icon colours single icons); the hex shows exactly in line, solid, duo, gloss, engrave, blueprint, sketch, sticker, retro, bauhaus, anime, pastel, brutal, shaded in the rest.
Animation: animate_icon(name, trigger loop|hover|once|inview|swap, format, style) returns code for the optional @withicons/motion package (loops, hover effects, icon-to-icon swaps); 3D styles (clay, glass, liquid, chrome, soft3d, luxe, skeuo ...) play it in 3D and soft3d returns 3-5 moves per icon.
Whole styles as files: https://withicons.com/downloads/with-icons-<style>.zip (every SVG + an offline viewer) and with-icons-all.zip.
Files: export_icon(name, style, format) makes files: svg, pdf, png, pptx, docx, favicons, app assets, Lottie, and animated ones for slides and docs: gif (plays in PowerPoint, Keynote, Google Slides, email, chat), apng, animated-svg, pptx-animated (a slide with the moving icon). Set background to the slide colour for GIFs. Pass out_dir to save files to disk.
Making slides and docs: call recommend_styles({ use: 'slides' }) first, then make the whole set in one call: export_icon({ names: [...], style, format: 'png', size: 512, colors: { ... }, out_dir }) (one colors set for every icon; the background stays transparent unless you set one). Embed PNG, not SVG (pptxgenjs slide.addImage({ path }) or python-pptx add_picture): a 512 px PNG stays crisp from 0.5 to 3 in on a slide; use size 1024 for larger or printed icons. 'pptx' is a one-slide deck with the icon to copy from, 'pptx-sheet' a deck of one icon in every style for choosing a look, 'pptx-animated' a ready slide with the moving icon: none of them merges into your own deck. Single-colour styles (solid, line: color sets the ink) match a brand hex exactly; gradient and shadow styles (clay, glass, liquid, soft3d, suite ...) shade the colours you give, so they never match a brand colour exactly.
Formats: svg, react, vue, svelte, angular, solid, html-class, web-component, data-uri. Packages: @withicons/react|vue|svelte|angular|solid|web|classes|core|static|motion|dynamic (web = <with-icon> element, classes = <i class="with with-home"> CSS icons); every framework package, <with-icon> and the class loader carry every style. Raw files of the newest styles live in companions: @withicons/core-plus, soft3d, holiday (SVG + node data), static-plus (prebuilt SVG, sprites), classes-plus; recommend_styles names the package per style. Names and common aliases both work (e.g. "delete" -> trash).
